extracted.intended_audience: readers/subscribers of The Mathematician; amateur and professional mathematicians and problem-solvers (19th-century mathematical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Provide complete solutions to posed mathematical exercises (geometry, algebra, calculus) suitable for publication in a mathematics periodical; solutions should be correct, clear, and often concise or elegant. The page collects multiple problems with submitted solutions and editorial remarks on their quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance of solution
rubrics_metrics.description: "The solutions of the proposer and Mr. Joseph Paul are very elegant and are omitted with much regret."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial note values 'elegant' solutions; elegance is singled out as a desirable quality (even when omitted for brevity), implying that concision, cleverness or aesthetic simplicity are positively regarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good solutions / general merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases recurring throughout: "Good solutions have also been received from..." and "Good solutions were received from..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors mark certain submissions as 'good', indicating an overall qualitative judgement based on correctness, clarity, and perhaps novelty; the page lists and acknowledges authors of submissions judged 'good'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neat demonstrations / clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Neat demonstrations of this exercise have also been received..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Neat' solutions—those that are tidy, straightforward and clearly presented—are specifically praised; clarity and tidy structure are treated as positive evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / independent invention
rubrics_metrics.description: From correspondence about priority: "giving at the same time a full explanation as to its originality..." and discussion of the surprising coincidence of similar methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality and independent derivation are important editorial considerations; authors are expected to attest to the originality of methods and editors note cases of independent discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological economy / eliminating unnecessary quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory methodological hint within a solution: "taking the moments about F (so as to get rid of the normal pressure and the friction)".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions that simplify by choosing viewpoints or operations that remove extraneous forces/quantities (thereby simplifying algebra or mechanics) are presented as preferable—i.e., using smart choices of reference points or conserved quantities to streamline the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and correctness of algebraic/manipulative steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the published solutions, detailed algebraic eliminations, substitutions and derivations are shown step-by-step (e.g., eliminating x, y, z by cross multiplication, equating coefficients, deriving areas from equations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted solutions are expected to be mathematically complete and correct: show derivations, justify eliminations and substitutions, and reach final stated identities or numeric results. Partial or incorrect arguments would not be accepted as 'good' solutions.
